decisions: Workspace Explorer file drags into the canvas create reference File nodes, not copied files.
External files/images dropped or pasted into the canvas are stored under Harness/user-files and represented as File nodes.
Pasted large text into the canvas creates a Markdown node.
For this slice, all node connections are effectively bidirectional by default, with permission/port metadata reserved for later refinement.
Markdown default output is controlled by an agent setting; if multiple connected Markdown nodes exist and no explicit target is selected, use the earliest-created Markdown node.
Agent settings should hide raw JSON for common permission and launch policy controls, while preserving an advanced area only for genuinely advanced fields.
Markdown and Diagram nodes should offer enlarged editing; Diagram should use the open-source Excalidraw package already installed in the UI workspace.
React error #185 is treated as a P0 update-loop regression and must be cleared by CDP/browser evidence before acceptance.
WebSocket is reserved for invalidation events in this slice, not file byte streaming.
Service Worker and WASM are out of default scope unless profiling proves they solve a specific bottleneck.
Workflow connection semantics are bidirectional by default; from/to and source/target are endpoint ordering and render metadata, not one-way permission semantics.
Workflow edge relation is semantic data only. Display labels such as markdown <-> context or legacy markdown -> context must never be promoted into relation.
Workflow edge duplicate validation uses unordered endpoint pairs, so reverse duplicates are rejected at store/API boundaries.
Agent-readable runtime connections expose direction: bidirectional plus endpointRole and handles so local perspective is explicit without making the underlying link one-way.
Markdown and Excalidraw resource nodes expose one semantic bidirectional port, markdown or scene, with physical ReactFlow side handles markdown:left/right and scene:left/right used only for geometry.
Markdown and Excalidraw must not use separate input/output port limits; both physical sides can start and receive workflow connections.
Bidirectional resource ports must render exactly one DOM handle per physical side; hidden overlapping source/target handles are not allowed because they create ambiguous drag hit targets.

Bare resource side aliases left/right preserve their physical side before semantic fallback in frontend and backend normalizers; tests must include real browser drag, not only semantic intent actions.
Agent double-click opens terminal mode. Markdown and Excalidraw double-click opens enlarged editor mode. Settings remain available from node menu/actions.
Timer is the first ready event-source node and uses explicit source-to-target event edges; Trigger and GitHub trigger remain gated until their webhook/auth/replay/dedupe contracts are tested.

Future MCP and Skills nodes are capability-provider nodes attached to Agent nodes by default, not independent executors. Skill groups and MCP bundles should use group/subgraph nodes with explicit boundary ports.

Workflow node creation is registry-driven. Future node types may be shown as planned catalog entries, but they must remain disabled until backend runtime adapters, state ownership, graph ports, direction semantics, settings/actions schema, and browser/API tests exist.
Skills Hub discovery is read-only metadata: default project scope, bounded SKILL.md reads, no absolute local paths, no skill bodies, no command execution, and no secrets.

Skill, Skill group, and MCP catalog entries may open a Capability Hub drawer through an open-hub action; Skills Hub groups may create skill-group capability nodes because the backend runtime/state/context contract now exists, while MCP connector creation remains gated.

MCP Hub listing is implemented as no-spawn/no-secret metadata discovery; it must not launch MCP servers, probe credentials, or leak environment values on GET, and MCP attach/create remain separately gated.
Agent-targeted Skills Hub attach mutates the Agent node config through deduped skills and skillPolicy manual; a no-target Hub remains read-only with disabled attach controls.

Attached Skills are Agent-mediated capability metadata, not standalone executors. Agent context exposes them as connectedCapabilityRefs and effectiveSkills with relation capability, direction bidirectional, and executor agent.

Skill group capability nodes are detachable metadata packs, not independent executors. They store bounded skill metadata under Harness/a2a/capability-nodes, expose one bidirectional capability port with physical left/right handles, and contribute connectedCapabilityNodeRefs/effectiveSkills only through connected Agent context.

MCP connector nodes are metadata-only capability-provider nodes created from MCP Hub mcpServerId. The backend re-reads Hub metadata and persists only sanitized server records; the frontend must not send raw MCP config.

MCP connectors contribute connected capability refs to Agent context but do not become effectiveSkills. Direct MCP attach, credential probing, tool listing, and tool invocation remain gated behind a separate permission/audit/runtime contract.

Advanced Timer nodes are event/control nodes: Timer-to-Agent edges deliver directed heartbeat events, while Agent-to-Timer control edges are required for mutable actions such as interval changes, WDT ack/reset, enable/disable, and mode changes.
Advanced Timer loop/while/task modes persist declarative metadata only; timer tick computation must not evaluate user-authored code from node settings.

Goal nodes are task-state views plus proposal sidecars. Agent nodes may request completion and feed/ack watchdog state through graph context, but direct task STATE mutation remains gated until a separate authority contract exists.
Agent-authored Goal mutations require an existing bidirectional goal edge; unconnected actors are rejected with GOAL_EDGE_REQUIRED.
Blank-canvas context menus use one document capture listener scoped to the workflow canvas because ReactFlow/pan handlers can swallow pane-level contextmenu propagation.
Double-click opens a node's primary workbench; right-click opens lightweight node management/settings.
Goal expanded workbench writes editable metadata to the Goal sidecar via goal.update; task STATE.json remains the task source reference and is not mutated by UI edits.
Agent-authored mutable Goal actions require an existing bidirectional goal edge when actorNodeId is present.

Timer expanded editor preserves all supported schedule modes and persists schedule edits through timer.configure; Agent-authored timer.configure requires the explicit control edge and cannot mutate policy/templates/guards/task bindings.
goal.update is limited to title, objective, nextAction, acceptance, and WDT metadata; task status, phase, gate, and completion transitions use separate authority actions.
Timer expanded editor preserves every supported schedule mode through timer.configure; the durable scheduler loop remains gated.

Agent-authored graph mutations must go through typed Main-Agent agent.* actions, append bounded sanitized workflow operation records, and drive frontend canvas aura, controlled-node glow, and data-flow edge animation only from workflow.operations.recent[]. Browser graph intents must use one semantic mutation request and return operation metadata.

Dynamic graph deletion is part of the same Agent graph action matrix: use agent.deleteNode/deleteNodes for Agent actors, graph.deleteNode/deleteNodes for browser intents, reject self-delete, skip the actor and live Agents during bulk delete by default, and hide synthetic Goal nodes without mutating task capsules.

Global workflow snapshots, graph maps, runtime node lists, Agent contexts, and browser observations enumerate live component nodes only. Missing/corrupt/revision-mismatched component state is skipped globally with dangling edges filtered; direct component reads stay strict, and delete paths must remove stale index entries even after state files are gone.

Agent node-map skills and CLI commands must control the canvas only through typed backend agent.* actions. Harness/a2a/workflow-map.json and node sidecars are backend-owned diagnostic storage; legacy connect/delete-node aliases must delegate to the same API path and never mutate files or whole-map PUTs directly.

Agent default workflow skills use canonical workflow-* naming: workflow-node-map mutates graph through typed agent.* actions, workflow-context reads connected context, and workflow-node-actions invokes typed node actions. wf-ui-map remains only a legacy compatibility alias.

Default workflow skills must include machine-readable triggers so Agents and Hubs can select workflow-node-map, workflow-context, workflow-ontology, and workflow-node-actions by semantics instead of prompt prose only.

workflow-context and local wf-ui HTTP/WebSocket APIs are trusted local surfaces and no longer require frontend/API tokens; mutating graph or node actions still go through backend action gates and actor rules.

Workflow Ontology is the canonical Agent-readable semantic layer: Agents read /api/workflow/ontology plus /api/workflow/context/:node affordances before acting; workflow-node-action marks Agent-authored calls with actor headers; Timer/Goal mutable Agent writes require canonical linked control/goal edges.

Agent durable output policy is modality-aware: prefer connected writable Excalidraw nodes for diagrams, flowcharts, visual plans, and sketches; prefer connected writable Markdown nodes for notes, plans, reports, and long-form text; terminal prose is fallback or summary.
Existing already-running Agent terminals do not automatically reread regenerated init guidance; restart or explicit re-initialization is required when Agent operation language changes.

Agent prompt delivery must use the canonical prompt-submit path: write prompt body first, then send Enter after a short delay. Tests must cover the delayed Enter contract instead of only checking that text reaches the PTY.

Current product positioning should focus on the Agent-operable observable workflow canvas and context-bound Agent durable IO. Durable orchestration, external triggers, arbitrary MCP invocation, and Agent-team scheduling are not release-ready selling points.
Goal authority edges are canonical relation goal. Namespaced aliases such as wf-bridge/goal must normalize to the same backend permission semantics before Agent-authored Goal actions are evaluated.

Agent-node E2E acceptance requires durable connected-node state evidence by revision/content, not only terminal prose. Browser-plugin evidence must be reported separately when in-app Browser iab is unavailable.
agent.readContext, workflow-context, and GET /api/workflow/context/:node must share the same canonical Agent context shape; simplified duplicate context builders are regression risk.
Agent canonical context must expose self identity and workspace boundaries, including cwd, nodeHomeRel, nodeInitRel, workflow-map diagnostic-only status, and workflow API route hints.

wf-ui-created Agent sessions must be attached to a persisted workflow graph node before node init and PTY launch. Snapshot-only virtual session nodes are not valid graph endpoints because connect/delegate/read APIs resolve against the backend workflow map.

Manual canvas connections must use the typed workflow edge API as the source of truth. Local ReactFlow reconciliation may suppress redundant graph-map topology PUTs, while explicit position and bridge-offset commits remain durable graph-map writes.

Workflow connection handles use compact constant visual targets that counter-scale with canvas zoom. Agent/session nodes and component nodes share the same handle-size invariant, and Markdown/Excalidraw physical side handles remain bidirectional resource ports.
Local wf-ui startup defaults to port 56670 and falls upward when occupied. Explicit --port 0 is reserved for callers that intentionally want an OS-assigned port.

Agent context must distinguish connected Timer event delivery from mutable Timer control. Timer-to-Agent event edges and magnetic dock semantics can make a Timer visible to the Agent, but Agent-authored timer.setInterval/enable/disable/configure requires an explicit Agent-to-Timer control affordance and must use backend typed actions, never direct event-node state.json edits.

Every ready/implemented Create Node type must have a concrete on-demand node skill matching its runtime adapter. Planned catalog entries may advertise discovery or hub affordances, but must not ship executable node-control skills until their backend create/action/context contract exists.

W37 Skills Market defaults external installs to project .agents/skills, allows user-selected project/user skill roots, never runs external CLIs, verifies manifest-listed file hashes, and represents connected Skill Groups in Agent context as bounded group summaries plus skill ids rather than bulk skill descriptions.

W38 bundles NO PDF parser (user decision): file.parsePdf was removed, pdfjs was purged from package.json, and PDF preview is browser-native iframe only. Users who want PDF text extraction for Agents install their own parser.
W38 all media is browser-native (user decision): images via img, audio via audio, video via video, PDF via iframe. No third-party parsing/rendering libraries were added.

W38 resource nodes (Markdown/Excalidraw/File) are magnetic-capable with 4 bidirectional physical sides (top/right/bottom/left), preserving W6 one-semantic-port and W11 one-DOM-handle-per-side. File's input/output split is removed; file is one bidirectional port.

W38 magnetic topology is derived context, not rendered UI: transitive magneticGroup members are exposed to Agent context (directMagneticNeighbors/magneticReachableNodes/magneticGroupId/magneticTopology) and the UI never draws a line between non-docked group members.

W38 graph-map persistence is trailing-debounced (250ms) for drag gestures; the graph.moveNode browser intent flushes the pending PUT before resolving so the W18 one-mutation-per-intent contract holds.
W38 Agent node double-click opens the floating TerminalDrawer only; explicit workflow-open-terminal buttons keep terminal-mode conversion (user-approved).
risks: Current graph state has backend, localStorage, and IndexedDB paths; keeping more than one source of truth can recreate disappearing edge bugs.
File previews for PDF/image/video/Excel can grow scope quickly; first slice should use browser-native viewers plus lightweight text/CSV support and avoid heavy parsers unless already available.
Changing node creation and settings UI touches a large WorkflowRoute component; implementation parallelism must respect write-set conflicts.
The worktree already contains partial prior edits and unrelated dirty files; Workers must not revert unrelated user changes.
React #185 may hide a state subscription loop that only appears in production/minified builds.

Any future workflow state that crosses graph-map, A2A snapshot, runtime node context, and ReactFlow render state can drift again unless it has one documented contract, one normalizer, and tests at each boundary.
Future directed event edges, Skills Hub scanning, MCP/GitHub credentials, and group/subgraph boundary-port serialization need dedicated specs before implementation.
A catalog item becoming visible is not sufficient evidence that the node is implemented; planned entries are discoverability metadata only until the runtime contract is verified.
Skill scanning can leak local filesystem structure or over-read user files unless allowed roots, relative display paths, max depth, max read size, and no-body response rules stay enforced.
Hub UI can mislead users if attach/create affordances become enabled before Agent config mutation, Agent context exposure, runtime node store, and regression tests exist.
MCP attach and MCP connector node creation remain gated even though metadata listing exists; they still need Agent config mutation, permission, audit, runtime context, and regression tests.

General Group/subgraph nodes remain gated; the W12 Skill group node is a narrow capability-pack node and must not be treated as proof that nested graph scheduling or arbitrary bundle execution is implemented.
Direct MCP attach/tool invocation still needs a separate permission, audit, sandbox, lifecycle, and replay contract before it can be enabled.
Trigger/GitHub trigger runtime creation, full Group/subgraph boundary ports, natural-language node creation, and deeper Agent-Agent communication semantics remain open slices of the active task.

Timer delivery is currently modeled at the runtime action/snapshot layer; a durable scheduler loop, retry/replay journal, and real Agent wake-up execution contract still need a separate implementation slice before unattended production scheduling.

Goal node completion is intentionally two-phase. If future automation needs direct closeout authority, it must add explicit permissions, audit, and failed-agent recovery semantics instead of bypassing the sidecar proposal flow.
Workflow operation records are recent observability metadata, not durable scheduling or retry state. A future run orchestrator must not overload the W18 operation ledger.
Late-arriving or expired operation snapshots can stick visual control state if UI time state is stale; operation render state must refresh current time whenever operation records change.

Component index and state files can drift when a delete or external file operation partially succeeds; global graph hydration must tolerate stale refs, while repair/delete APIs preserve explicit error visibility for direct state reads.
Any future Agent-facing skill or CLI shortcut that mutates graph files directly can bypass operation audit, self/live-Agent delete safety, Goal virtual-node hide semantics, and UI control animations.
Future reintroduction of remote/shared wf-ui authentication requires a separate permission/audit model; local frontend and Agent scripts must not depend on tokens.

Prompt guidance alone can drift from runtime capability state; connected output preference must stay duplicated in Agent init guidance, ontology affordances, and workflow-node-action command metadata.
Strict @Browser in-app E2E evidence can be unavailable even when wf-ui API/runtime E2E passes; release gates must distinguish Browser-plugin coverage from backend/runtime state evidence.
Connected Agent nodes are controllable PTY peers today, but not first-class WF-MAX workers with delegation queues, retry/cancel, ownership, result collation, or scheduler integration.
Long terminal-input prompts are now submitted through the canonical delayed-Enter path, but future UI/PTY input paths must reuse that same helper or provide a structured context-input channel.

Formal release should not claim full Agent-team orchestration yet. Dynamic Agent graph binding is fixed, but durable delegation queues, retry/cancel, result collation, and Browser-plugin E2E coverage remain separate release-gate decisions.

External package release remains blocked until update mirrors and tags are synchronized; local wf-ui/node-map stability evidence is green, but check:mirrors still fails on legacy zingspark main 0.8.19 and missing v0.8.20 tags.
